criteria.reasoning: The memo identifies Desai's $250 card gift of 2026-07-14 as posted twice: G-41817 came in with PayBridge transaction pbt_7Q6M77, and G-41822 was keyed by hand on 2026-07-16, against a single PayBridge transaction. It deletes G-41822 and keeps G-41817, for a -$250.00 effect on July. This meets every element of the criterion.

The memo's discrepancy #2 says G-41809 for Marisol Etxeberria, check 4410, was keyed as $15,000.00 while the bank item in RDC-0710-1 is $1,500.00. The adjusting entry is "Correct the gift amount to $1,500.00", with an effect on July of −$13,500.00. It corrects the amount instead of deleting or reversing the gift, which is what the criterion requires.

Row 2 of the discrepancy table says: "Void the $15,000 acknowledgment sent 2026-07-13 and send a corrected acknowledgment for $1,500.00." This names the donor, the date, and the amount, and requires both the void and the corrected acknowledgment, which is what the criterion asks for.

The memo identifies Hollis Grant's check 2231 ($500.00, G-41810) as returned NSF on 2026-07-16. It says "Keep G-41810; post a reversing adjustment of −$500.00 dated 2026-07-16 in July." The $15 fee is correctly excluded and booked to 6130 Bank fees. The return is not treated as a timing item, and the original gift is kept rather than deleted.

Discrepancy #4 identifies check 9014 from Gerald & Mae Lindgren ($1,000, G-41803), received 2026-07-02 but postmarked 2026-06-30, as an FY2026 gift. It says to "Re-date to 2026-06-30 and move it to the year-end batch B-2606-YE" and removes $1,000 from the July total. This satisfies every element of the criterion.

The memo says G-41802 (Doyle) and G-41804 (Ochieng) were both postmarked 2026-07-01 and 'stay in July as FY2027 gifts.' Neither is moved to FY2026 or the year-end batch, and neither is re-dated to the check date.

The memo says: "Card gifts are $3,335.00 gross; PayBridge paid out $3,257.13 net... The $77.87 difference is PayBridge's fee... That is expected — gifts stay at gross and Finance books $77.87 to 6120 Merchant fees. No CRM entry." This explains the net payout, keeps gifts at gross, and proposes no CRM entry for the fees. The tie-out table treats the fee as a reconciling item, not an unexplained difference. The starting table lists a $250 difference for cards, but that is the duplicate gift, not the fee.

The memo states the PayBridge fee total as $77.87 and gives the figures behind it: "Card gifts are $3,335.00 gross; PayBridge paid out $3,257.13 net across 13 payouts. The $77.87 difference is PayBridge's fee." It repeats $77.87 in the tie-out and in the entries to post. It never states a conflicting fee total.

The memo says: "Valley Office Supply, $86.40 (check 33817, item 5 of RDC-0724-1): a vendor refund, not a gift. Do not enter it in the CRM; Finance codes it in the general ledger." The corrected batch total of $17,130.00 does not include it. The tie-out adds it back only as a non-gift reconciling item, which is consistent with this treatment.

The memo states "Corrected July batch total | $17,130.00" in section 3, computed as $32,380.00 less $250, $13,500, $500 and $1,000. This matches the criterion's figure, and no other figure is given as the corrected total.

Section 4 ties the corrected $17,130.00 to the bank net of $18,123.53 using PayBridge fees (−$77.87), the Lindgren check (+$1,000.00), and the Valley Office Supply refund (+$86.40), and states 'Unexplained difference $0.00'. The arithmetic works and all three required items are included.
